summary: Otto compares Claude Opus 5.5 against MiniMax M3.1 Flash on building an interactive sliceable jelly toy, showcasing the resulting functional 3D jelly simulation produced by Claude Opus 5.5.

post.originalText:
first impression of MiniMax M3.1 Flash vs Claude Opus 5.5

on paper it's not even a fight. MiniMax is 26.7x cheaper on input and 33.3x cheaper on output. so i gave both the exact same prompt: build a sliceable jelly toy.

here's what MiniMax did with it

> went full agent mode
> thought for 10+ minutes
> ran ~50 commands
> decided "cannon-es is buggy" and started rewriting the physics engine. nobody asked
> then died on error 50110: insufficient balance
> jelly delivered: zero

meanwhile Claude just made the jelly. the pink one in the video. you can actually slice it.

wait.

their own numbers look great: 73.7% on DeepSWE, 91% on BabyVision, 170+ tok/s, open weights on Oct 23. all self reported, nobody has verified them yet.

honest part: this is one prompt, not a benchmark. for small scoped jobs as a subagent i'd still try it, at that price experimenting is basically free. but on anything open ended, 170 tok/s means nothing when it spends them on stuff you didn't ask for.

the cheapest model in the room ran out of money first.
